notes: Identity independently checked in supplied canonical text: title Why Do We Hate Hypocrites? Evidence for a Theory of False Signaling; authors Jillian J. Jordan, Roseanna Sommers, Paul Bloom, David G. Rand; DOI 10.1177/0956797616685771; Psychological Science research article, copyright 2017. Full 13-page primary research report, including methods, results, discussion and references; not an abstract or secondary report. No PDF path supplied; no acquisition or rendering performed. Study 4, pp. 8–9, three-condition between-subjects design, positive-evaluation composite averaged over four primary measures and vignettes. Candidate omnibus: F(2, 449) = 35.62, p < .001, printed partial eta-squared ηp2 = .137. Candidate traditional versus honest hypocrites: t(301) = −7.69, p < .001, d = −0.88. Candidate traditional hypocrites versus control transgressors: t(300) = −6.84, p < .001, d = −0.79. Candidate honest hypocrites versus control transgressors: t(297) = 0.88, p = .382, d = 0.10. These are candidates only, not assigned target values. The locators and descriptions do not specify a contrast or explicitly select the omnibus. Requested effect metric alone does not establish the target; printed ηp2 is partial eta-squared, not unqualified eta-squared. No conversions performed. The final analyzed Study 4 sample is 452 participants with unique IP addresses who evaluated all vignettes (457 survey completions); this is a candidate N for the common three-group omnibus model. It cannot establish the N for an unspecified two-group comparison. Final group counts are not printed in the inspected Study 4 methods/results, so no pairwise analytic N is derived from degrees of freedom or recruitment targets. Only assigned unfinished fields examined; other fields/sides are placeholders. done means inspection completed, not target correspondence verified.
